channel.title: The Night Desk
channel.description: News for the Graveyard Crew — true crime, breaking news, and the stories that keep you up at night.

item.title: Rex Ryan surrenders in Nashville, charged in Broadway hit-and-run that injured two pedestrians
item.description: Former NFL head coach and current ESPN analyst Rex Ryan surrendered to Metro Nashville Police on Nov. 11 and was booked on misdemeanor charges tied to a Nov. 5 hit-and-run on Broadway, where police say a truck ran over two pedestrians' feet and one leg, the driver argued with the victims, and then drove away.

item.title: Southwest Michigan man missing since July was last seen traveling with his dog, Raven
item.description: Ashton Coon, 23, has been missing since July 2026. He was last seen traveling on foot with his female German Shepherd, Raven, and may be in the Three Rivers, Mendon, or Sturgis area. The St. Joseph County Sheriff's Office is asking anyone with information to call 269-467-9045.

item.title: FBI offers $25,000 reward in Paige Moore cold case — Broken Arrow teen's 2012 disappearance now ruled a homicide
item.description: Paige Summer Moore, 17, walked out of her Broken Arrow, Oklahoma home in the early morning of July 10, 2012 and was never seen again. Police have now reclassified her case as a homicide, detectives are hunting a dark green 2002 Chevrolet Tracker, and the FBI is offering up to $25,000 for information leading to her recovery or the arrest and conviction of those responsible.

item.title: More than 300 Italian schools evacuated after emailed bomb threat; officials say no concrete danger found
item.description: A single emailed bomb threat reached about 6,300 Italian state schools on Nov. 11, prompting precautionary evacuations at more than 300 buildings. Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara called the alerts presumed hoaxes, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks found no evidence of concrete danger, and no explosive device was reported found.

item.title: New witness leads to arrest in 2013 Phoenix cold case killing of security guard Jeffrey Bellemare
item.description: Phoenix police say a witness who was a teenager in 2013 came forward in early 2026 and identified Joe Alexander Gerardo, 43, in the Nov. 29, 2013 killing of security guard Jeffrey Bellemare, 59. Gerardo was arrested Nov. 3 in Globe and is held on $2 million bond on first-degree murder.

item.title: FBI offers $20,000 reward for convicted fugitive Jose Del Carmen Garcia Martinez
item.description: FBI Denver announced a $20,000 reward on Nov. 10 for Jose Del Carmen Garcia Martinez, 62, who fled during his Arapahoe County trial, cut off his ankle monitor, and was convicted in his absence of sexually assaulting a 15-year-old girl with disabilities.

item.title: Explosive device in a backpack kills a police officer in Oviedo, Spain
item.description: One Spanish National Police officer was killed and another seriously wounded on Nov. 10 when an explosive device in a backpack went off in Oviedo as officers responded to a shooting. Authorities said there was no indication yet of a terror link, and the suspect fled.

item.title: Terry Brisk cold case — ten years unsolved, reward raised to $50,000
item.description: Terrence "Terry" Brisk, 41, was shot with his own hunting rifle on his parents' property near Little Falls, Minnesota, on Nov. 7, 2016. No one has been arrested in ten years. On Nov. 6, 2026, Morrison County Sheriff Shawn Larsen raised the reward to $50,000 for information leading to an arrest and conviction.

item.title: Russell Brand sentenced to 10½ years for rape and sexual assaults
item.description: Russell Brand was sentenced Monday at Southwark Crown Court to 10 years and six months in prison for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others between 2004 and 2009. He must serve two-thirds of the sentence before release.

item.title: Russell Brand back at Southwark Crown Court for sentencing after rape conviction
item.description: Russell Brand, 51, returned to Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday to learn his sentence, four days after a jury convicted him of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Prosecutors asked for 12 to 15 years on the rape count.

item.title: Krakow Main Square gunman dies in hospital after attack that killed six
item.description: Michał Oksiński, 24, who opened fire in Krakow's Main Square on Saturday, killing six people and wounding 15, died in hospital early Monday. Authorities say he is also believed to have killed his parents and his sister at the family home before driving to Krakow.

item.title: Vienna homecoming shooting — eight more charged, two fugitives still on the run
item.description: At a Nov. 5 press conference, Dooly County Sheriff Craig Peavy, GBI Director Chris Hosey and FBI Atlanta SAC Marlo Graham announced eight more people charged in the Oct. 4 Vienna, Georgia homecoming block-party shooting that killed Ja'Quavion Jackson and Macaleb Jackson. Six were arrested; Brexton Esamuel Gaston, 19, of Cordele and Vanravious Rashad Williams, 34, of Perry remain at large and are considered armed and dangerous.

item.title: Spirit Halloween shooting — teen publicly named, charged with two murders; prosecutors seek adult trial
item.description: The Solano County District Attorney's Office has publicly identified Monte Smith, 17, as the suspect in the Oct. 30 Spirit Halloween store shooting in Fairfield that killed pregnant mother of four Constance Hages, 31, and wounded six others. Smith faces two murder counts with a multiple-murder special circumstance. At his first court appearance on Nov. 4, a judge ordered him to remain in juvenile detention without bail and postponed his arraignment to Nov. 13; prosecutors are asking a judge to move his case to adult court.

item.title: Moss Landing shooting — two dead, two injured near a closed California beach; victims not yet identified
item.description: Two people were killed and two others injured in a shooting along Jetty Road near Moss Landing State Beach early Monday, the Monterey County Sheriff's Office said. The victims have not been identified, no motive has been released, and investigators say there is no active threat to the community.

item.title: Fairfield Spirit Halloween shooting — 17-year-old arrested in killing of pregnant woman; six others wounded
item.description: Fairfield police arrested a 17-year-old at his Suisun City home Monday in the Oct. 30 shooting inside a Spirit Halloween store that killed 31-year-old Constance Hages, who was pregnant, and wounded six others. The teen faces murder and attempted murder charges; police say they identified him within hours through surveillance footage but withheld it to protect the arrest.

item.title: Boulder house-party shooting — CU student killed, another critical, police seek people seen on video
item.description: A 19-year-old University of Colorado student was killed and another 19-year-old student was critically injured in a shooting at a Halloween house party in Boulder's University Hill neighborhood late Saturday. Police have not arrested a suspect and are asking partygoers for photos, video and tips.

item.title: Spain train collision — 4 Americans among 69 dead, all but three victims now identified
item.description: Four U.S. citizens were among the 69 people killed when a high-speed Renfe train slammed into the rear of a stationary Iryo train near Urda, Spain, on Oct. 28. Authorities said late Sunday that all but three of the victims have now been identified.

item.title: Halloween night in East Lansing — 5 wounded in two shootings off the MSU campus
item.description: Five people were wounded in two separate shootings in East Lansing on Halloween night, Police Chief Jennifer Brown said at a Nov. 1 press conference. Four victims are stable and the fifth victim's status was unknown to police. Both shootings happened off campus and, MSU's president said, did not involve anyone affiliated with the university.

item.title: Learjet goes down in a Palm Beach County neighborhood — all 9 aboard killed
item.description: A Learjet 60 flying from Austin to the Bahamas crashed near Greenacres, Florida, around 12:50 p.m. Sunday, killing all nine people aboard. Recordings captured the crew reporting turbulence and ice before a descent that topped 32,000 feet per minute. The NTSB is leading the investigation.

item.title: Halloween night in Dallas — 4 dead, 15 injured in three Deep Ellum shootings
item.description: Four people were killed and 15 injured in three separate shootings in Dallas's Deep Ellum entertainment district early Sunday. Police Chief Daniel Comeaux says detectives are still working to determine whether the shootings were linked.
